notes:
ACCOUNT SUMMARY
- Enterprise fintech/bank. Evaluating Redwood primarily for regulated internal LLM workloads with strong change-management requirements.
- Pushing for VPC (customer-controlled networking) with auditability/immutability guarantees for model metadata + customer-visible release notes.
- Procurement stage: security + GRC review in progress; legal queued.

FIRMOGRAPHICS / CONTEXT
- HQ: North America (primary ops US). Initial workload must remain in US region (prefers us-east). EU expansion “later, maybe Q3”.
- Deployment: VPC Private strongly preferred. Hosted API considered only for non-prod experimentation.
- Typical regulated expectations: ticketable change notices, retention, and evidence for audits.

PRIMARY USE CASES (CURRENT)
1) Internal support + ops summarization
   - Summarize support interactions, internal incident threads, and policy updates.
   - Needs citations / traceability back to internal sources.
2) Compliance & risk analysis assistant (non-customer facing)
   - Drafting and summarizing regulatory guidance + internal control mappings.
   - Sensitivity: wants strict access controls, audit trails.
3) Document search / retrieval + embeddings
   - They already run embeddings elsewhere; evaluating consolidated platform.

WORKLOAD CHARACTERISTICS
- Traffic: moderate steady-state with spikes during incident/compliance cycles.
- Latency target: “sub-2s first token for chat-style responses” for internal users; batch jobs can be slower.
- Throughput: expects dedicated capacity sizing; wants predictable cost envelope.
- Model behavior consistency is critical: “We can’t have the same prompt produce materially different output without a record of what changed.”

PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS (HARD)
- Formal model/version change-management
  - Customer-visible changelog/release notes per model version.
  - Deprecation notices with explicit timelines + replacement model/version.
  - Emergency hotfix path must still preserve audit history (no silent edits).
- Auditability / immutability
  - Wants “who changed what, when” for:
    - model metadata changes (context window, quantization, routing/fallback policy changes that can affect output)
    - publication/approval actions for release notes
  - Requires tamper-evident history (append-only or signed events) + retention controls.
- Retention controls
  - Asked for minimum 1 year retention for changelog + audit logs; GRC suggested 7 years for some audit artifacts. They asked if Redwood can support longer retention tiers.
- RBAC
  - Needs clarity on internal Redwood roles: who can edit metadata vs who can approve/publish customer-visible notes.
  - Asked for separation of duties (“editor != approver”) and an emergency publish workflow with post-facto review.
- SIEM integration
  - Wants audit events exportable (fields suitable for Splunk). Requested sample event payloads / field mapping.
- Console/API surfaces
  - Wants API to fetch the resolved model_version used for a request and a stable URL to the relevant changelog entry.
  - Asked for a machine-readable feed (JSON/RSS acceptable) for ingest into internal change-management tooling.

MODEL / PLATFORM PREFERENCES
- Open to open-weight models; emphasis on stability and rollback over “latest model”.
- Wants pinning by version_id and visibility into compatibility notes (tool/function calling, context window, tokenizer changes).
- They specifically asked whether runtime upgrades can change performance/behavior and how that is reflected in release notes.

SECURITY REVIEW NOTES (FROM CALL)

  - “We need immutable release notes for any model changes—our auditors ask for a record of what changed and when.”
  - “If there’s a rollback, that needs to show up as a new entry, not an edited past entry.”
  - “Don’t just say ‘performance improvements’—tell us compatibility impact and whether we need to re-run our validations.”
